All variables are defined using static or templated strings, with no command substitutions, dynamic evaluations, or network operations at the top level. The `source` arrays reference GitHub release URLs using the declared `pkgver`, which is a standard and expected pattern. There are no calls to `curl`, `wget`, `eval`, or any other potentially dangerous commands during sourcing. The `package()` function contains executable code, but it will not be executed during `makepkg --printsrcinfo` and is therefore out of scope for this safety gate. LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided `.SRCINFO` file contains metadata for the `dffy-render-mermaid-bin` package, which is a binary plugin for the `dffy` diff viewer. It specifies two sources — one for x86_64 and one for aarch64 — both pointing to release assets hosted on the official GitHub repository (https://github.com/amalucelli/dffy). The URLs are HTTPS-secured and match the declared upstream, reducing the risk of tampered or unexpected sources.

Each source has a corresponding SHA-256 checksum (`sha256sums_x86_64` and `sha256sums_aarch64`) that ensures the integrity of the downloaded binaries. The package does not use `SKIP` for checksums, and the sources are not VCS-based, so verification is straightforward and secure. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, suspicious scripts, or network operations in the metadata.

The package follows standard AUR packaging practices: it declares architecture support, dependencies, optional dependencies, conflicts, and provides appropriate metadata. The `noextract` directive is used appropriately for binary-only packages, and the `!strip` and `!debug` options are reasonable for prebuilt binaries. No malicious or suspicious behavior is present.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AUR binary package with verified sources and no malicious indicators</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches prebuilt binary releases from the official GitHub repository of the project (https://github.com/amalucelli/dffy), specifically versioned release assets over HTTPS. The sources are properly scoped to the declared upstream, and the filenames are constructed predictably using the package version and architecture. The checksums for both x86_64 and aarch64 are explicitly defined and match standard practice for binary packages.

The build process consists only of extracting the downloaded tarball using `bsdtar` and installing the binary, license, and README files into standard system directories with appropriate permissions. No compilation, patching, or dynamic fetching occurs during the `package()` function. There are no uses of `eval`, `curl|bash`, `wget`, or other high-risk constructs. The package installs only its own files and does not modify system configuration or execute external scripts.

All operations are consistent with standard AUR packaging practices for a binary distribution. The use of `noextract` and architecture-specific source handling is necessary due to identical filenames in architecture-specific archives and does not introduce risk. The package depends only on `glibc` and optionally `dffy-bin`, which is expected for a plugin. No obfuscated code, suspicious network activity, or unauthorized file access is present.
</details>
<evidence>
